issues.legal_issue: An outgoing attributable to a discontinued business cannot be deducted against income from other businesses unless the discontinued business was part of the same business carried on during the relevant accounting year.
material_facts: The taxpayers claimed a deduction for part of mesne profits payable for their use of a theatre after their lease had expired.
The theatre business had closed before the accounting year for which the deduction was claimed.
The taxpayers argued that the theatre business was part of their continuing business of exhibiting films through other theatres.
The court found that the taxpayers had not established that the theatre business was part of that continuing business.
issues.conclusion: The claimed outgoing was not allowable as a deduction against income from the taxpayers’ other business activity.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(1) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, business income is taxable under that provision only where the business is carried on in the relevant year. An outgoing attributable to a discontinued business cannot be set off against income from other businesses if they are distinct and independent; it may be allowed against the continuing business only if the discontinued venture was part of that same business.

predicates.business_income_deduction_claim: The taxpayer claimed a business-income deduction for an outgoing attributable to one business against income from business activity.
predicates.claimed_business_discontinued_before_acc: The business to which the outgoing was attributable had ceased before the relevant accounting year.
predicates.claimed_business_is_distinct_from_contin: The business to which the outgoing was attributable was not part of the business activity continued during the relevant accounting year.

issues.definition: If a taxpayer claims a business-income deduction for an outgoing attributable to a business that ceased before the accounting year and that business was distinct from the continuing business, the deduction is disallowed.

issues.legal_issue: Whether ventures of the same general character constitute one business depends on their factual and commercial unity, and their common character alone does not establish that unity.
material_facts: The taxpayers conducted film-exhibition ventures at several theatres.
The theatres were operated independently and had separate identifiable books of account.
Opening or closing a theatre did not affect the operation of the other theatres.

Although the results of the separate ventures were incorporated into accounts at a head office, there was no evidence establishing unity of control and management, interrelation, common staffing, or that closure of one theatre affected the rest of the business.
The tribunal concluded that the theatre for which the outgoing was claimed had been an independent business.
issues.conclusion: The taxpayers did not establish that the theatre venture was part of a single business of exhibiting films through multiple theatres.
issues.legal_principle: Whether different ventures constitute one business is a mixed question of law and fact. Under Setabganj Sugar Mills Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, the inquiry considers interconnection, interlacing, interdependence and unity, including unity of control and management, use of the same agency or staff, interrelation of the ventures, the nature of their transactions, and whether one can be closed without affecting the others. Ventures of the same character are not, for that reason alone, necessarily one business.

rule.if: business_unity_assessment and same_character_ventures and separate_identifiable_books and closure_of_one_venture_does_not_affect_others and no_evidence_of_business_interconnection

predicates.business_unity_assessment: The court was assessing whether multiple ventures counted as one business for a business-income deduction claim.
predicates.same_character_ventures: The taxpayer carried on ventures of the same general character.
predicates.separate_identifiable_books: The taxpayer maintained separately identifiable accounts for the ventures.
predicates.closure_of_one_venture_does_not_affect_o: The operation of the other ventures was not affected when one venture was closed.
predicates.no_evidence_of_business_interconnection: The taxpayer did not establish facts showing interconnection, interdependence, or unity among the ventures.

issues.definition: When ventures of the same character are assessed for business unity, separate accounts, unaffected operations upon closure of one venture, and no evidence of commercial interconnection mean that a single business has not been established.
